prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and market equilibrium in differentiated-product industries, which made empirical industrial organisation a quantitative tool for competition and regulatory analysis

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part on B005 crediting Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn. I changed the wording and my reasoning, not the part or the names. The chair asks for one test applied to all four leading candidates, so I state mine. Did the work change what can be credibly known? Has it been validated in use or in evidence? Is the credit attributable within three names? How much does it add beyond a prize already awarded? On B005, the random-coefficients demand framework with endogenous prices made substitution patterns, market power and welfare measurable from market data. Merger review, antitrust, regulation, trade, health and environmental work have exercised it for about three decades. The three names are the authors of one jointly written core, and Pakes also anchors the dynamic strand. I see no prior prize that covers it. Under the same test, B014 is original and mature, but its causal identification is weaker and its overlap with the 2024 institutions prize has to be argued. B027 is the most conceptually original and has the cleanest attribution, but its validation is indirect and it sits next to the 2022 prize. B030 has design-based evidence and a clean trio, but its persistence and magnitude debates and its shift-share identification are not settled, and its overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes is debated. This is my own weighing. Five members naming B005 is not evidence of merit and I do not use it that way. I verified none of the claims about prior prizes or replication records, and I rely on the openings for them.
statement.case_against: My strongest reservation is unchanged. This is a methods and measurement prize without one headline substantive finding. If the Committee judges that a toolkit ranks below a conceptual mechanism (B027) or a policy-relevant substantive finding (B014, B030), my case is weaker. The three-name cap forces a contestable boundary. Bresnahan and Reiss are left out, and so are Benkard and Levin on the dynamic strand. The citation therefore has to be tied to demand and equilibrium estimation, not to the whole empirical-IO tradition. BLP-type estimates depend on functional form, instruments and implementation. I read that as evidence of scrutiny, but it limits how much settled empirical knowledge the prize can claim. I also concede that my field proximity to market design and auctions may make me value structural, theory-to-data methods more than a neutral reader would.

responses.point: Hassler prefers B014 narrowly. He separates how given electoral and constitutional rules shape fiscal policy from the 2024 prize on long-run institutions, and he says he would move to B005 rather than defend B014 as it stands if the Committee judges the overlap decisive.
responses.response: I accept the distinction he draws. It is a fair argument that the 2024 overlap is a weight, not a bar, and I have not used it against B014. My concern is the one he and Fredriksson already concede: the cross-country identification is weaker than the validation B005 has had through repeated use. His B014 case also rests partly on within-country and state-capacity evidence that the openings do not set out in detail. If the Committee goes to B014, I would support a citation that does not overclaim causal findings, and I would take Fredriksson's Persson-Tabellini core seriously as the fallback if Besley's strand is judged too close to 2024. I cannot settle that from the supplied evidence. For now I rank B014 as my first alternative because the programme is coherent, mature and cleanly attributed.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B027 because it is conceptually original, durably influential and cleanly attributed to Kiyotaki and Moore. He concedes that its empirical validation is weaker than B005's documented use and that B005 would be a strong prize on merit.
responses.response: I agree with his attribution and originality arguments, and I weigh them seriously. In round 1 I leaned on the 2022 overlap, but he and Boppart argue that bank runs and intermediation differ from collateral-constrained borrowers, and I now treat that overlap as a modest weight, not a reason to rank B027 lower. The difference between us is the test. If conceptual originality is the main test, B027 may come first. If the test is what changed what can be credibly known, plus validation in use, B005 does better, as he himself concedes. I cannot show that either test is the correct one, so I do not claim B027 is weaker. I keep it as an alternative. I also agree with him that adding Gertler or Gilchrist would blur the citation.

responses.point: Teorell prefers B005 but frames the citation around both demand estimation and dynamic industry models. He accepts that Levinsohn versus Bresnahan depends on what the citation is for.
responses.response: I agree that the citation should be built on the BLP estimator, and I agree on keeping Levinsohn. I am cautious about writing dynamic industry models into the main clause. Pakes's dynamic work is a real strand, but the dynamic-estimation credit also runs through Benkard and Levin, who are outside the three names. A broad dynamic clause could imply credit that the laureate set does not carry. I would accept a short secondary reference to Pakes's work on dynamic industries if the Committee wants it. My wording keeps the part to demand and market equilibrium. This is a drafting preference, and I do not treat it as a dispute about the scientific merit.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers B030 because it answers a substantive question about who bears the costs of technological and trade change, and because the Autor-Dorn-Hanson trio is cleaner at the three-name boundary than B005's Levinsohn-versus-Bresnahan choice.
responses.response: She is right that the B030 trio is cleaner at the boundary. Where I differ is that the B005 boundary question is about the scope of the citation, not about who authored the core, and five members now name the same three. The shared test also bears on maturity. She and Dreber concede that the persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects and the shift-share identification remain debated. For B005 the debate is about implementation within a framework that has been used heavily for decades. Whether the policy relevance of B030 should outweigh that is a legitimate judgement, and I have not verified the replication record independently. I would support B030's Autor-Hanson-Dorn trio, not Katz, if the Committee chose it. That is not my preference, and I keep it off my alternatives only because I can name just two.

responses.point: Friberg revised his third name from Bresnahan to Levinsohn in round 1, while keeping Bresnahan's market-power inference tradition as a different, important contribution.
responses.response: This closes the main attribution dispute I raised in round 1, and I am glad he moved. I withdraw the open question I raised about Bresnahan or Reiss replacing Levinsohn. I would keep them out unless the Committee deliberately widens the citation to the earlier empirical-IO tradition and changes the credited names with it. I also note his field disclosure and mine. Both of us work near this field, so our agreement should not be read as independent confirmation.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats a measurement-and-estimation contribution as meeting the bar against conceptual (B027) or substantive (B014, B030) discoveries. I have no agreed way to compare them beyond the common test stated above.

Whether a citation tied to demand and equilibrium estimation will be accepted as the right scope, or whether the Committee prefers a broader empirical-IO citation that would bring in Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard or Levin.
How much weight the 2024 and 2022 prizes should carry against B014 and B027. I cannot verify the extent of overlap from the supplied evidence, and members' statements differ.
How sensitive BLP-type estimates are to implementation and instruments, and how far that should qualify the claim of settled empirical knowledge. I have not verified this independently.
Whether my closeness to market and mechanism design leads me to overweight structural methods.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for B005, B014 or B027. My collaborators and affiliations (Teytelboym, Trapp, Biró, Svensson, Ehlers, Erlanson, Martinello, Östling, Lindqvist) are not among the credited names. I disclose that my research field, market and mechanism design with auctions, is adjacent to B005's structural industrial organisation, which may bias me toward it. I am a Lund colleague of Enflo, who also prefers B005, and I am an SSE affiliate alongside Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. Friberg and Strömberg also prefer B005, so their agreement with me is not independent confirmation. I do not read these ties as requiring recusal and I do not adjudicate them. The 2020 presentation speech and my committee tenure are in my profile. The speech was an Academy text and does not show my preferences for 2026.
